articles.summary: Ardent Health Marks Expansion of Specialty Care in New UT Tyler School of Medicine wroberts Wed, 09/02/2026 - 08:18 New academic and clinical hub reflects joint venture partnership's commitment to expanding access to care in East Texas BRENTWOOD, Tenn. and TYLER, Texas (Sept. 2, 2026) – Ardent Health (NYSE: ARDT), a leading provider of healthcare in growing mid-sized urban communities across the U.S., today marked a milestone in its East Texas partnership as UT Health East Texas expanded specialty care into the new UT Tyler School of Medicine Building in Tyler – the first time patient services and physician training share a single hub in the region. The building now houses UT Health East Texas women's health, pulmonary, orthopedic, imaging and surgical care alongside the region's first medical school. The expansion builds on the joint venture Ardent formed with The University of Texas System in 2018 to expand access to care and grow the local physician workforce in a region facing persistent health challenges. Northeast Texas, a 35-county area of roughly 1.6 million people, would rank among the least healthy states in the country if measured on its own, according to research led by UT Tyler. As rural communities across the U.S. continue to face hospital closures and shrinking access to care, the partnership is working to build a different future for East Texas. Since the joint venture formed in 2018, Ardent has: Invested more than $315 million in capital across UT Health East Texas, exceeding its original five-year commitment ahead of schedule. Grown the employed and affiliated provider network to roughly 640 providers, a 116% increase. Supported the expansion of graduate medical education from about 39 residents and fellowships in 2018 to more than 270 today and approval to grow to 323. Strengthened financial and clinical performance, including multiple UT Health East Texas facilities earning "A" Safety Grades and Top Hospital recognition from The Leapfrog Group annually. "At Ardent, we invest for the long term in the communities we serve, and we're proud of what this partnership with The University of Texas System has built in East Texas – a stronger local workforce, more specialty care and a medical school training the next generation of physicians," said Dave Caspers, president and CEO of Ardent Health. "It's a powerful example of what's possible when a community, a university and a health system pull in the same direction to make healthcare better." With nine hospitals, more than 90 clinics and the region's only Level 1 trauma center, UT Health East Texas offers a range of clinical settings and specialties to help train East Texas physicians. UT Tyler's School of Medicine, which welcomed its inaugural class in 2023, has consistently drawn students with deep local roots: 95% of its first class, 85% of its second and 90% of its third have ties to the region – a strong indicator it is producing physicians likely to practice locally. “The opening of the School of Medicine Building is not only a defining moment for our students and faculty, but also for the East Texas communities we serve,” said UT Tyler President Julie V. Philley, MD. “The addition of clinical services within the building is a testament to the power of our partnership with Ardent Health through UT Health East Texas. By integrating education and patient care, we are creating new opportunities for learning, innovation and improved healthcare outcomes throughout the region.” "When this partnership began, the vision was a healthier future for East Texas, and the School of Medicine Building brings it full circle," said Donald Baker, president of UT Health East Texas and Ardent's Lone Star Region. "Education and patient care now sit side by side, expanding care for patients and training the physicians that will care for this region tomorrow." About UT Health East Texas UT Health East Texas provides care to thousands of patients each year through an extensive regional network that includes nine hospitals, more than 90 clinics, the Olympic Plaza Tower, 13 regional rehabilitation facilities, two freestanding emergency centers, regional home health services, an EMS fleet of more than 65 ambulances and four helicopters, and a comprehensive eight-trauma center care network, including the region's only Level 1 trauma facility. As a partner with The University of Texas System, UT Health East Texas is uniquely positioned to provide patients with access to leading-edge research and clinical therapies while training and educating the next generation of physicians and other health professionals. About Ardent Health Ardent Health (NYSE: ARDT) is a leading provider of healthcare in growing mid-sized urban communities across the U.S. The Company delivers care through its subsidiaries, which include 30 acute care hospitals and more than 280 sites of care with over 2,000 employed and affiliated providers across six states. Anchored by a shared operating model and a commitment to investing in innovative services and technologies that improve quality, access and experience, Ardent is focused on delivering strong clinical outcomes and improving the health of the patients and communities it serves. articles.summary: Ardent Health Hospitals Earn Recognition in U.S. News & World Report’s 2026-2027 Best Hospitals Rankings wroberts Tue, 09/15/2026 - 08:11 Thirteen facilities across Ardent markets recognized for excellence in specialties, procedures and conditions BRENTWOOD, Tenn. (Sept. 15, 2026) – Ardent Health (NYSE: ARDT), a leading provider of healthcare in growing mid-sized urban communities across the U.S., today announced that 13 hospitals across its network earned recognition in U.S. News & World Report’s 2026-2027 Best Hospitals rankings, the publication’s 37th annual assessment of hospital quality. The honors include a Best Regional Hospital designation, regional specialty rankings and 34 High Performing ratings across procedures and conditions. A High Performing rating is the highest distinction a hospital can earn in U.S. News’ Procedures & Conditions ratings. The annual ratings are designed to help patients and healthcare providers make informed decisions about where to receive care for challenging health conditions and elective procedures. “These rankings are meaningful because they point to the work happening every day at the bedside and across our care teams,” said Dave Caspers, president and CEO of Ardent Health. “Across our organization, teams are focused on doing the fundamentals well – delivering safe, reliable care, supporting each other and continuing to improve for the patients and communities who count on us.” Ardent Health facilities earning recognition include: Hillcrest HealthCare System | Tulsa, Oklahoma Hillcrest Medical Center was rated High Performing in seven procedures and conditions: transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), heart bypass surgery, pacemaker implantation, leukemia, lymphoma and myeloma, heart attack, diabetes, and heart arrhythmia. Oklahoma Heart Institute TAVR program ranked No. 19 in the nation among more than 800 TAVR programs and No. 1 in Oklahoma. Hillcrest Hospital South was rated High Performing in back surgery, specifically spinal fusion; ear, nose and throat surgery; diabetes; and kidney failure. Tulsa Spine & Specialty Hospital was rated High Performing in back surgery, specifically spinal fusion. Lovelace Health System | Albuquerque, New Mexico Lovelace Medical Center was named a Best Regional Hospital and ranked No. 2 in New Mexico and the Albuquerque metro area. The hospital was also rated High Performing in eight procedures and conditions: abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, heart bypass surgery, knee replacement, back surgery, pacemaker implantation, leukemia, lymphoma and myeloma, heart attack, and heart arrhythmia. Lovelace Rehabilitation Hospital ranked No. 1 in rehabilitation in both New Mexico and the Albuquerque metro area. Lovelace Westside Hospital was rated High Performing in pneumonia. Lovelace Women’s Hospital was rated High Performing in prostate cancer surgery. BSA Health System | Amarillo, Texas BSA Hospital was rated High Performing in abdominal aortic aneurysm repair and prostate cancer surgery. Physicians Surgical Hospital-Quail Creek was rated High Performing in back surgery, specifically spinal fusion. UT Health East Texas | Tyler, Texas UT Health Tyler was rated High Performing in abdominal aortic aneurysm repair, pacemaker implantation and prostate cancer surgery. Portneuf Health | Pocatello, Idaho Portneuf Medical Center was rated High Performing in abdominal aortic aneurysm repair and heart attack care. The University of Kansas Health System St. Francis Campus | Topeka, Kansas The University of Kansas Health System St. Francis Campus was rated High Performing in colon cancer surgery, hip fracture and knee replacement. Seton Medical Center Harker Heights | Harker Heights, Texas Seton Medical Center Harker Heights was rated High Performing in heart attack care. “Quality and safety are built through disciplined, daily work – using clinical data to guide decisions, strengthening care processes and supporting consistent evidence-based standards across our hospitals,” said FJ Campbell, MD, chief medical officer of Ardent Health. “These recognitions reflect the commitment of our physicians, nurses and care teams to improve outcomes and deliver safe, high-quality care for the patients and communities we serve.” U.S. News evaluated nearly 4,500 hospitals across 14 adult specialties and 23 procedures and conditions. To determine the Best Hospitals rankings and ratings, U.S. News analyzed each hospital’s performance using objective measures including risk-adjusted mortality, preventable complications and patient experience. The specialty rankings and Procedures & Conditions ratings measure patient outcomes using data from more than 800 million patient care records.
